title: bug: start_step accepts a worker that never claimed the row
description: DEFECT observed 2026-09-13 alongside task-2a7e0f5b (split out of that card by its architect). util/enforcement.ts assertWorkerOwns (and assertContextFetched) return early when task.assignedWorkerId is null, so moe.start_step on an UNASSIGNED WORKING row succeeds for any registered, non-DEAD worker. tools/startStep.ts then writes { implementationPlan, status: WORKING } to the task and touchWorker(params.workerId, { status: CODING, currentTaskId: task.id }) — the worker record points at a row it never claimed while the task stays unassigned and no execution attempt is opened (a one-way back-pointer). That is how worker-c8e523ea ended up CODING on task-9e851 with a stale currentTaskId during the incident. Expected: a step can only be started by the worker that owns the row (task.assignedWorkerId === workerId) — or, for an unassigned row, start_step must refuse with a retryable STATE_CONFLICT that points at moe.claim_next_task { taskId }, never stamp the worker. Keep the change daemon-only and inside the ownership guard + startStep; do not touch attempts (task-2a7e0f5b owns attempt lifetime). Check complete_step / complete_task for the same early-return hole and cover them in the same change if they share it.
definitionOfDone: moe.start_step on an unassigned WORKING task is refused with a STATE_CONFLICT whose nextAction is moe.claim_next_task { taskId }, and the caller worker record is left untouched (status and currentTaskId unchanged)
moe.start_step by a worker other than task.assignedWorkerId is refused with NOT_ALLOWED exactly as today; the owner path is unchanged and all existing startStep tests stay green
complete_step and complete_task either already refuse a non-owner on an unassigned row or are fixed under the same rule, with a test per tool proving the refusal
docs/MCP_SERVER.md states the rule under moe.start_step; npm test and npx tsc --noEmit pass in packages/moe-daemon

implementationPlan.description:
Add the claimed-row guard in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/enforcement.ts (CRLF file: edit with the Edit tool, not Serena, and keep CRLF). Put it directly after assertWorkerOwns, before the 'Attempt fencing' banner.

(1) `export const TASK_NOT_CLAIMED = 'TASK_NOT_CLAIMED';` (grep confirms the name is unused).

(2) `export function assertWorkerHoldsTask(task: Task, workerId: string | undefined, toolName = 'unknown'): void`. If `workerId` is truthy and `task.assignedWorkerId` is falsy, throw `new MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, message, context, TASK_NOT_CLAIMED)`. Otherwise call `assertWorkerOwns(task, workerId, toolName)` unchanged. That keeps a foreign owner as NOT_ALLOWED with owner/caller context, and keeps a missing or empty workerId on the legacy path (tolerated, with the once-per-(task,tool) warning).

context = `{ taskId: task.id, workerId, retryable: true, nextAction: { tool: 'moe.claim_next_task', args: { taskId: task.id, statuses: ['WORKING'], workerId }, reason } }`. claim_next_task's schema requires `statuses`. 'WORKING' is correct because every caller already refused a non-WORKING row; say so in the doc comment.

message: McpAdapter sends only code, message and {tool, codeName}. MoeError.context never crosses the MCP wire, so the message alone must be actionable (same convention as util/claimGuards.ts): `Task ${task.id} is not claimed by any worker, so ${workerId} cannot call ${displayToolName(toolName)} on it. Claim it first with moe.claim_next_task { taskId: "${task.id}", statuses: ["WORKING"] }, then retry — this is a RETRYABLE refusal (context.retryable), NOT a fatal error.`

Error handling: the guard only throws a typed MoeError. It catches nothing, logs nothing, reads no state and writes nothing. McpAdapter's existing MoeError branch logs the rejection and maps it to a JSON-RPC error, so no new try/catch is needed anywhere, and nothing may swallow the refusal.

Doc comment, WHY only: in the 2026-09-13 incident both ownership guards returned early on an unassigned WORKING row. start_step then stamped worker-c8e523ea CODING with a currentTaskId for a row it never claimed, with no attempt opened. assertWorkerOwns itself deliberately keeps its unassigned no-op, because its other callers rely on it: report_blocked on an unassigned task, submit_plan, qa_approve/qa_reject, request_replan, acquire_resource and wait_for_resource.

Unit tests in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/enforcement.test.ts (LF). Add a new `describe('assertWorkerHoldsTask')` using the file's makeTask helper:
(a) Unassigned task, caller 'worker-x', toolName 'moe.start_step'. Throws MoeError with code MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT and codeName 'TASK_NOT_CLAIMED'. context toEqual `{ taskId:'task-1', workerId:'worker-x', retryable:true, nextAction:{ tool:'moe.claim_next_task', args:{ taskId:'task-1', statuses:['WORKING'], workerId:'worker-x' }, reason: expect.any(String) } }`. The message contains 'moe.claim_next_task', 'task-1' and 'moe.start_step'.
(b) toolName 'complete_step' renders as 'moe.complete_step' in the message.
(c) Unassigned with workerId undefined, and with '', does not throw.
(d) Assigned to the caller does not throw.
(e) Assigned to 'worker-a', caller 'worker-b': throws codeName 'NOT_ALLOWED' with context owner 'worker-a' and caller 'worker-b'.
(f) Assigned with workerId undefined does not throw.
Leave the existing 'assertWorkerOwns still no-ops on an unassigned task' test untouched: it pins that the other callers keep their tolerance.

Land this export BEFORE any importer (steps 2-4). A named ESM import of a missing export fails at link time for every peer running the suite.

implementationPlan.description:
Document the rule in docs/MCP_SERVER.md (LF, keep LF; use Edit, not Serena). Do not add or rename any `### moe.*` heading: src/util/taskTimeBudgetDocs.test.ts matches the headings against getTools().

(1) DoD 4. Under `### moe.start_step`, after the get_context blockquote, add a **Claimed row required** note covering:
- When the call carries a `workerId`, the task must be assigned to that worker.
- On a `WORKING` task whose `assignedWorkerId` is `null`, the call is refused with `STATE_CONFLICT` (`-32002`, codeName `TASK_NOT_CLAIMED`) before any other guard, including the get_context check.
- Nothing is written: the step stays `PENDING`, and the caller's worker record (`status`, `currentTaskId`) is not touched.
- The refusal is retryable. Claim the row with `moe.claim_next_task { taskId, statuses: ["WORKING"], workerId }`, call `moe.get_context`, then retry. The message names the claim call because MoeError context does not cross MCP; in-process callers also get `context.retryable: true` and `context.nextAction`.
- A caller whose `workerId` differs from a set `assignedWorkerId` is still refused with `NOT_ALLOWED`.
- A call without a `workerId` (the plugin `/ws` path, legacy clients) keeps the old tolerance.

(2) `### moe.complete_step` Notes: add one bullet. The same claimed-row rule as `moe.start_step` applies: the step stays `IN_PROGRESS` and nothing is recorded.

(3) `### moe.complete_task` Notes: add one bullet. The same rule applies, and the refusal comes before the attempt is moved to `finalizing` and before the REVIEW write. The task stays `WORKING` with no verification persisted, and the caller's worker record is untouched.

(4) **Ownership & Ordering**. Line 111 says every guard is a no-op when `assignedWorkerId` is `null`, which is no longer true. Amend it: the no-op still holds for calls without a `workerId` and for `submit_plan`/`qa_approve`/`qa_reject`, but `start_step`, `complete_step` and `complete_task` refuse a supplied `workerId` on an unassigned row (`TASK_NOT_CLAIMED`, see `moe.start_step`). Describe that refusal in prose after the guard table, not as a table row: the sentence before the table says every guard failure is `NOT_ALLOWED` (-32003), and this one is -32002.

implementationPlan.description:
Prove red, run the regression suite, then self-review.

(1) Red proof without breaking the shared checkout. Follow Serena memory `pattern-red-proof-by-scratch-tree-mutation-vitest`.
- Build a scratch tree OUTSIDE the repo holding packages/moe-daemon/{src,package.json,tsconfig.json,vitest.config.ts}, with a node_modules junction to the repo's.
- Target files: src/util/enforcement.test.ts, src/tools/startStep.test.ts, src/tools/completeStep.test.ts and src/tools/completeTask.test.ts.
- Run `none` first. Its counts must equal the repo's.
- Then apply one mutation at a time, restoring from pristine and sha-verifying between runs:
  - old-startStep, old-completeStep, old-completeTask: each swaps in `git show HEAD:packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/<file>.ts`.
  - guard-noop: the body of assertWorkerHoldsTask reduced to `assertWorkerOwns(task, workerId, toolName)`.
- Expected:
  - Each old-tool swap turns ONLY that tool's new cases red, with behavioural failures (a promise that resolved instead of rejecting, or 'CODING' where 'IDLE' was expected).
  - guard-noop turns all the new tool cases red, plus unit cases (a) and (b).
  - Every pre-existing case stays green.
- Run `none` again last.
- Record the mutation-to-red map in the step note.
- Teardown: delete the junction FIRST with `(Get-Item <junction> -Force).Delete()`, confirm the repo's node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs still exists, then rm -rf the scratch tree and cmp the repo targets against the final sources.

(2) Regression, from packages/moe-daemon:
- `npx vitest run src/util/enforcement.test.ts src/tools/startStep.test.ts src/tools/completeStep.test.ts src/tools/completeTask.test.ts src/tools/enforcement.integration.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.race.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts src/__e2e__/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`
- Then the full `npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit`. Both must exit 0 (DoD 4); report the exact command and exit code in complete_task.verification.
- Under fleet load, rerun a failing file that is unrelated to this change on its own before calling it a flake. Never report a red run as green.

(3) Adversarial self-review:
- Error handling: every new refusal is a thrown typed MoeError that fires before any write (updateTask, touchWorker, setAttemptPhase, postSystemMessage). No try/catch was added or widened, so nothing can swallow the refusal and leave a half-applied row or worker.
- `grep -rn "assertWorkerOwns(" src --include=*.ts` still shows the other callers unchanged: submitPlan, qaApprove, qaReject, reportBlocked, requestReplan, acquireResource and waitForResource.
- A workerId of '' or undefined stays on the legacy path.
- Handlers run under the state mutex (McpAdapter runExclusive), so no write can interleave between the guard and the handler's own writes.
- `git diff` shows no whole-file EOL flips. CRLF: enforcement.ts, completeTask.ts, startStep.test.ts, completeStep.test.ts. LF: startStep.ts, completeStep.ts, enforcement.test.ts, completeTask.test.ts, docs/MCP_SERVER.md.
- Report every path you touched in complete_step.modifiedFiles.
- Leave dirty paths that belong to peers alone: never stage, stash or revert them.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Make assertWorkerOwns itself refuse unassigned rows. Rejected: seven other tools call it and rely on the unassigned no-op. report_blocked on an unassigned task is a documented seat-freeing path, and submit_plan, qa_approve/qa_reject, request_replan, acquire_resource and wait_for_resource have their own flows, so the blast radius would go beyond this card.
2) A boolean option on assertWorkerOwns. It works, but it hides a stricter contract behind a flag at the call sites. A named sibling guard, assertWorkerHoldsTask, reads clearer and leaves assertWorkerOwns byte-identical.
3) Also refuse calls without a workerId on unassigned rows. Rejected: it breaks startStep tests that the DoD requires to stay green ('preserves legacy path when workerId is not supplied (null assignedWorkerId)' and the harness 'marks step as IN_PROGRESS', whose createTask defaults to assignedWorkerId null). It also breaks the plugin /ws and legacy-client contract. Such calls cannot stamp a worker record anyway, because touchWorker is a no-op for a falsy id.
4) Only drop the `|| params.workerId` touchWorker fallback. Rejected: a non-owner would still start or complete steps on an unclaimed row, and the DoD requires a refusal that points at the claim.
5) NOT_ALLOWED instead of STATE_CONFLICT. Rejected: the DoD asks for a retryable STATE_CONFLICT. The caller becomes entitled once it claims, which is the same reasoning as ATTEMPT_FINALIZING and ATTEMPT_RECONCILING in util/claimGuards.ts.
6) Put the constant in claimGuards.ts. Kept in enforcement.ts instead, next to the ownership guard it extends, as the card asks ('inside the ownership guard'). enforcement.ts never imports claimGuards.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- McpAdapter.ts:308-315 returns only code, message and data {tool, codeName}. MoeError.context (retryable, nextAction) is visible in-process only, so the refusal message must name the claim call itself; claimGuards.ts documents the same convention.
- claim_next_task requires `statuses`. An explicit `taskId` claim auto-registers an unknown worker (claimNextTask.ts:530-540).
- touchWorker (workerStore.ts:91) is a no-op for a falsy id, a missing record or a DEAD record.
- All three tools check status === WORKING before the ownership guard, so a refused row is always WORKING.
- complete_task calls no assertContextFetched. After the new guard, assertContextFetched's unassigned early return is unreachable from start_step and complete_step whenever a workerId is supplied, so that helper stays unchanged (qa tools use it).
- Prototype evidence: this exact rule was applied to a scratch copy of packages/moe-daemon (outside the repo) and the full suite gave 2001 passed with 0 behavioural failures. The 17 failures came only from inputs missing in the scratch copy: taskTimeBudgetDocs needs docs/, and the providerDescriptor contract needs scripts/moe-agent.sh. No existing test depends on the hole.
- File EOLs are mixed (see step 6). Memory says Serena edits flip LF files to CRLF, so use the Edit tool.

Following the nextAction re-claims the row; if a peer took it, the caller gets NOT_ALLOWED as today. An operator who calls moe-call with an identity on an unassigned row is also told to claim first.

completionSummary:
This fixes the defect where moe.start_step, moe.complete_step and moe.complete_task accepted a supplied workerId on an unassigned WORKING row and stamped that worker's record. It adds `assertWorkerHoldsTask` and `TASK_NOT_CLAIMED` to util/enforcement.ts as a strict sibling of assertWorkerOwns, which stays byte-identical so its 7 other callers keep the unassigned no-op.

Guard behaviour:
- A truthy workerId on an unassigned row gets STATE_CONFLICT (-32002, codeName TASK_NOT_CLAIMED), context `{taskId, workerId, retryable:true, nextAction:{tool:'moe.claim_next_task', args:{taskId, statuses:['WORKING'], workerId}}}`. The message names the claim call.
- Every other case goes to assertWorkerOwns: a foreign worker still gets NOT_ALLOWED, and no workerId (legacy) is still tolerated.

The three tools swap in the new guard in place (+2 -2 each). It runs before every write, and in complete_task before steps, verification, branch policy and setAttemptPhase('finalizing').

Tests (all +N -0):
- 6 unit cases.
- start_step: 3 cases. The refusal writes nothing (worker stays IDLE/null); the claim is refused before get_context; following nextAction.args through claim_next_task, then get_context, then the same start_step succeeds.
- complete_step: 1 case. Nothing is recorded and the worker is untouched.
- complete_task: 1 case. The task stays WORKING with no verification and the worker stays CODING/task-other.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md gets a Claimed row required note under start_step, a bullet each under complete_step and complete_task, and an amended Ownership & Ordering no-op sentence plus a prose paragraph.
